rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy (Residential Tenant Protections)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, meaning one of the listed at-fault causes (such as nonpayment of rent, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, criminal activity) or no-fault causes taken in good faith (owner move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court order, or demolition or substantial remodel).
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies (a right to occupy residential rental property for more than 30 days, excluding fixed-term leases of three months or less) in residential rental property in San Diego, including units in mobilehome parks, other than exempt properties.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; short-term residential occupancy; deed- or agreement-restricted affordable housing; housing subject to affordable housing subsidy agreements (not including Section 8); mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care and residential care facilities, adult residential facilities and non-profit transitional housing; school and college dormitories; units where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with a resident landlord; landlord-occupied single-family residences (renting no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs or two JADUs) and mobilehomes; two-unit properties where the landlord occupies one unit; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable property whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, if tenants received the required written exemption notice.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code §98.0704; §98.0703 (O-21647 N.S.; amended O-21769 N.S.)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.interaction_text: This Division protects the rights of tenants by requiring just cause for termination of a tenancy consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2, limiting the grounds for termination of a tenancy, requiring greater tenant relocation assistance in specified circumstances, and providing additional tenant protections. The rights conferred by this Division are in addition to any existing rights provided to tenants by state or federal law.

rules.title: Owner Move-In No-Fault Just Cause Conditions
rules.requirement: An owner may terminate for owner or family move-in only if the intended occupant moves in within 90 days after the tenant vacates and lives there for at least 12 continuous months; the notice must name the intended occupant and relationship to the owner and tell the tenant they may request proof. For leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023, this ground applies only if the tenant agrees in writing or the lease expressly allows it.
rules.key_value: move in within 90 days; occupy at least 12 continuous months
rules.coverage_text: Owners (natural persons with qualifying ownership interests) of covered residential rental property seeking possession for themselves or listed family members; does not apply if the intended occupant already occupies a unit on the property or a similar unit is vacant.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply if the intended occupant occupies a rental unit on the property or if a vacancy of a similar unit already exists at the property. Death of the intended occupant after moving in within 90 days is not a violation.
rules.penalty: If the intended occupant does not move in within 90 days or does not stay 12 continuous months, the owner must offer the unit back to the tenant at the same rent and lease terms and reimburse reasonable moving expenses in excess of relocation assistance paid.
rules.quoted_span: (E) Section 98.0704(b)(1) applies only if the intended occupant moves into the residential rental property within 90 days after the tenant vacates and occupies the residential rental property for at least 12 continuous months.

rules.title: Demolition or Substantial Remodel No-Fault Just Cause Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord terminating to demolish or substantially remodel must post any permit application at the property within three business days of submittal, secure required permits before issuing notice, and give a notice certified under penalty of perjury describing the work and duration, attaching permits, explaining why the tenant must vacate for at least 30 continuous days, and stating the tenant's right to re-rent if the work is not commenced or completed. Cosmetic improvements do not qualify as substantial remodel.
rules.key_value: tenant must be required to vacate for at least 30 continuous days
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of covered residential rental property seeking possession to demolish or substantially remodel.
